items.title: [allafrica.com] Somalia orders UAE ambassador out within 72 hours in diplomatic rift
items.content_html: Somalia’s government on Nov. 19 ordered the United Arab Emirates ambassador to leave within 72 hours and recalled its own envoy from Abu Dhabi after President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud accused the UAE of interfering in Somali affairs, backing armed groups and making port deals with regional administrations without federal approval. The UAE rejected Mogadishu’s accusations, calling its approach “escalatory and hostile,” and said it had already closed its embassy and withdrawn its diplomats in January after Somalia canceled bilateral agreements. The dispute involves UAE relations with Somaliland, Puntland and Jubaland, as well as disagreements within Somalia over constitutional changes and election arrangements. Parliament amended the constitution in March to extend presidential and parliamentary terms from four years to five; regional administrations and opposition figures rejected the changes. Somalia’s Supreme Court later ruled that the current leaders’ terms had expired and set deadlines for an election framework and polls.

items.title: [eldia.com.do] Car bomb in Villavicencio leaves more than 20 injured on anniversary of peace deal
items.content_html: On November 24, Colombia commemorated the tenth anniversary of the peace deal signed in Bogotá between the government and the FARC guerrillas. The day before, a car bomb exploded in Villavicencio, leaving more than 20 people injured. President Abelardo de la Espriella blamed the attack on FARC dissidents and ruled out negotiating with armed groups. The agreement ended more than half a century of conflict between the government and the guerrillas; more than 13,600 combatants laid down their arms. A decade later, the Kroc Institute estimates that 36% of the commitments have been fulfilled. The Office of the Ombudsman records 521 signatories killed, and the Armed Forces estimate that armed groups total around 29,000 members across 165 structures, compared with approximately 13,000 in 2022. After the FARC withdrew, the government failed to establish a sufficient presence in several areas, which were left vulnerable to disputes among other groups. De la Espriella has cut the budget of the Special Jurisdiction for Peace (JEP), the court created by the agreement, and ended talks with armed groups. Former president Juan Manuel Santos maintains that the problems stem from the failure to implement the agreement. At the request of the Colombian government and with the backing of the United States, the UN verification mission will stop monitoring rural reform; its overall mandate was renewed for one year.

items.title: [Bambu Lab Community Forum - Latest posts] Auto-detect the failed layer with the nozzle force sensor and resume (A1 / A1M)
items.content_html:
Problem
When filament stops feeding mid-print (clog, tangle, grinding), the printer keeps “printing” in the air. By the time you notice, the nozzle is several mm above the part and hours of printing are wasted. Resuming is possible in principle, but the hardest part is finding the exact layer where it failed. Measuring the part with calipers is slow and error-prone.

Proposal

  1. Add a “Resume from failure” function. With the failed part still on the bed, the printer probes several points on top of it with a cold nozzle, using the force sensor that the A1 series already uses for bed leveling. The slicer knows the model geometry, so it picks the probe points.
  2. From the measured heights the printer determines the last successfully printed layer.
  3. The printer offers: “Print stopped at layer N (Z = X mm). Resume from here?” and continues on the same part.

Optional: detect extrusion loss during printing (force sensor + filament motion data), pause automatically, and offer the same resume, so the part is still in good shape.

Why
It saves long prints and material, and it uses hardware the A1 / A1 mini already have.

Demand

  • The general request “Resume from Layer”: Feature Request: Resume from Layer
  • A community tool that already does manual resume, Layer Rescue: Layer Rescue: resume failed prints from any layer, even after a power loss

People clearly want this. Automatic layer detection would make it safe and easy for everyone.

items.title: [bbc.co.uk] UN climate summit ends without pact as fossil fuel dispute stalls talks
items.content_html: The COP31 United Nations climate summit in Antalya, Türkiye, ended on Nov. 22 without an overarching agreement after nearly 200 countries failed to resolve disputes over fossil fuels and climate finance. The talks ran about two days past their scheduled close, making COP31 the longest COP conference on record. The final draft omitted an explicit reference to fossil fuels, prompting the European Union, the United Kingdom, Panama and vulnerable island states to reject it. The draft referred indirectly to the 2023 COP28 commitment to transition away from fossil fuels but did not spell out a pathway or reaffirm the wording. Oil-producing countries, including Saudi Arabia and Russia, resisted explicit references to fossil fuels, while poorer countries objected that the proposal did not set concrete funding levels for adaptation. COP31 negotiations chair Chris Bowen said fossil fuels and finance were the main obstacles; summit president Murat Kurum said he would not put forward a replacement draft. Countries agreed on separate measures, including a program to support workers and communities through the energy transition and a plan to assess adaptation progress. More than 80 countries backed Türkiye’s proposed goal of raising electricity’s share of global energy use to 35% by 2035, but the goal was not part of an adopted overarching pact. UN climate chief Simon Stiell said he would seek advice on possible reforms to the consensus-based negotiating process. The next summit is scheduled for Addis Ababa.

Verdict: worse, cycling

The shipped feed is 39.0% wanted, down 5.2 points from 44.2% 4 weeks ago. 3 finding(s) have been open 3+ weeks, and gate-misses got worse while open: reported every week, none closed.

Fix next (a session can do these)

  1. The gate threw away 38.0% of the rejects you wanted (7 week(s) open, 11.8 → 38.0, worse). Read the wanted rejects from the named sources in feedback/, find what in quality_charter.txt or the gate prompt rejects them, and fix that one cause. Done when: wanted share of rated rejects under 10%.
  2. 5 categories are unmeasured (7 week(s) open). Find why rotate_review_categories() leaves these categories short: a 12-a-day batch can give every category the floor. Fix the rotation, not the quota. Done when: every category has 20+ ratings in 28 days.
  3. Places you want that the pool barely carries (7 week(s) open). Trace the place's own outlets through a run (feed failing, filtered, or unanchored) and fix what keeps them out of the pool; add a source only if none exists. Done when: the place is in 1%+ of the pool.

During the week of November 16–22, 2026, the aggregator completed 7 runs, fetching an average of 1,673 articles per run and delivering an average of 91 quality-passing articles per run. Across the week's deliveries, the category distribution was: ai-tech 126, news 105, climate 81, wellness 71, homelab 57, science 58, local 47, design 39, homestead 14, outdoors 14, and scifi 5. Articles are scored on a dimensional quality/relevance/local composite, weighted 0.25, 0.55, and 0.20 respectively. Over the trailing 14 runs, the pipeline's mean noise-to-signal ratio (articles fetched per article delivered) was 2.57, within a range of 1.15 to 3.37, indicating moderate filtering load with no notable outliers in the current window.

Feed changes this week included the addition of GN Civil Eats, GN Wildfire Today, GN Parents, GN Neuroscience News, Castanet.net (Canada), Climate Crisis (Coda Story), Common Dreams, FOSSIL HUNTRESS (listed twice), and GN Logging and Sawmilling Journal. Feed health shows 21 feeds with errors, including Civil Eats, GN Western Producer, GN AgWeb, Wildfire Today, and Neuroscience News; these warrant inspection, as several are recently added sources.

Feed discovery returned three identical candidates from passivehouseplus.co.uk ("Browse by category") with a score of 76.9, indicating a duplicate discovery result rather than three distinct sources. items.title: [thenews.com.pk] Battlefield use of AI weapons grows as Geneva talks leave rules unsettled
items.content_html: AI-enabled weapons are in use in conflicts in Ukraine, Sudan and the Middle East, while campaigners say armed drones that can independently select and strike targets have appeared in limited cases. The International Committee of the Red Cross says commanders must remain responsible for the lawful use of force. At U.N.-backed talks in Geneva, 128 countries agreed to develop an international instrument on lethal autonomous weapons over the next two years, but left open whether it would be legally binding. Around 100 countries had sought binding rules; the United States, Russia and Israel opposed that push, and the consensus-based forum allowed any member to block stronger language. The process is expected to examine which systems should be prohibited and which could be regulated. Government experts are to recommend the instrument’s form, including whether it should be binding. The International Committee of the Red Cross says commanders must remain responsible for the lawful use of force, including when weapons act with little or no human oversight.

items.title: [ScienceDaily] Time may be far stranger than we realize. Scientists have a way to test it
items.content_html: Time may be far stranger than we realize, and scientists have proposed a way to detect clocks experiencing multiple flows of time simultaneously. Using atomic clocks with dramatically enhanced sensitivity, researchers hope to reveal a never-before-observed quantum effect that could transform our understanding of time and gravity.

items.title: [ScienceDaily] A 50-year-old theory about evolution may have been wrong all along
items.content_html:
🔭 ✏️

A decades-old theory suggesting that evolution protects its most important genes from mutations has been dealt a major blow. An extensive new analysis of mutations in bacteria and yeast found no evidence that essential genes mutate less frequently than other genes. Researchers say earlier studies may have been misled by harmful mutations that disappeared through natural selection before scientists could detect them.

items.title: [time.com] Ebola death toll in Congo exceeds 5,700 as response lags
items.content_html: An Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 11,700 confirmed cases and 5,700 deaths as of Nov. 19, making it the country’s largest and deadliest. Cases have also been reported in Uganda, Kenya and Nigeria. The Bundibugyo strain is driving the outbreak, and no approved vaccine or targeted treatment is available for it. Health workers say early cases can be difficult to identify because initial symptoms resemble those of other illnesses. Late detection, population movement and mistrust of response teams have hindered containment, while attacks on health workers and burial teams have further complicated the response. On Nov. 17, health workers in Butembo, North Kivu, escalated a month-long strike over unpaid wages and bonuses, halting even minimum service at treatment centers.

items.title: [lemonde.fr] Costa’s EU budget draft cuts regional funds for first time
items.content_html: European Council President António Costa’s revised 2028-34 budget proposal would cut EU cohesion funding for the first time, reducing regional development funding by €8 billion compared with the Irish presidency’s previous draft. The change affects a coalition of 17 southern and eastern member states, including Poland, Italy and Spain, that had opposed cuts to cohesion funding. Costa’s proposal also reduces allocations for competitiveness, defence and external action. It leaves direct farm subsidies unchanged from the previous draft, but France says the proposed Common Agricultural Policy funding still fails to guarantee farmers’ income support. The revised framework cuts €204 billion from the European Commission’s original plan. EU leaders will discuss the proposal at a special summit in Brussels on November 26-27. The European Parliament must also approve the eventual budget, and its chief budget negotiator, Siegfried Muresan, has warned that lawmakers may withhold consent over the reductions.
